reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a periodic rectangular pulse train with robust-standardized amplitude ~2.47, baseline at 0.0, and near-zero noise. Each cycle consists of a sharp vertical rise to the upper extreme (≈2.47), a flat high plateau lasting ~1/3 of the cycle, then a sharp vertical drop back to baseline. The period is consistently 98 points across all candidates, as confirmed by window_cycles: candidate 0 shows exactly 1 cycle in 98 points; candidates 1 and 2 show 3 cycles in 294 points (98×3); candidate 3 shows 5 cycles in 490 points (98×5). Pulse width is stable at ~33 points (≈1/3 of 98), and inter-pulse intervals are ~65 points. No curvature or smooth transitions—edges are near-vertical, indicating step-like behavior. Baseline is perfectly flat (median = 0, MAD = 0) and stable across all references. Minor slope differences (e.g., +0.0084 in ref 1, −0.0051 in ref 3) are negligible relative to pulse magnitude and likely reflect tiny drift over long windows, not structural deviation. All candidates exhibit identical peak/trough morphology: instantaneous rise/fall, flat top/bottom, no overshoot or ringing. Noise is effectively absent (roughness = 0, curvature = 0). Acceptable variation includes tiny linear trends over multi-cycle windows (<0.01 per point) and exact alignment of pulse edges varying by ≤1 index due to sampling—no variation in amplitude, duty cycle, or shape is observed across reliable candidates.

reference_profiles.description: Single clean rectangular pulse: zero baseline until index ~8, sharp rise to 2.47, flat top until index ~21, sharp drop back to zero, remaining flat to end. Exactly one full cycle in 98 points. No noise, no trend, perfect symmetry.

Three identical rectangular pulses spaced evenly over 294 points. Each pulse rises sharply, holds flat for ~33 points, drops sharply. Slight positive linear trend (~0.0084 per point) visible across the full window but does not affect pulse shape or amplitude. Edges align closely with expected 98-point spacing.

Three identical rectangular pulses, same morphology as ref 1 but with zero observable trend (slope_per_point = 0). Pulses are perfectly aligned to 98-point intervals, flat baseline, no distortion. Slightly cleaner than ref 1 due to absence of drift.

Five rectangular pulses over 490 points. Pulses maintain identical shape and amplitude. Exhibits slight negative linear trend (−0.0051 per point), causing very minor baseline tilt across the long window, but pulse heights remain fixed at 2.47 and edges remain sharp. Timing remains precise at 98-point intervals.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for single-cycle queries (e.g., short windows ≤100 pts) due to its purity and lack of drift. For multi-cycle queries (≥200 pts), prefer reference 2 as the gold standard—it confirms the pulse pattern repeats identically without trend. Use reference 1 or 3 only when matching query length closely (e.g., ~294 or ~490 pts) and when small monotonic drift is present; their drift is acceptable if pulse shape, amplitude, and timing match consensus. Never use drift magnitude alone to reject a candidate—only reject if pulse morphology (rise/fall sharpness, plateau flatness, amplitude) deviates.
uncertainties: Whether the near-zero MAD reflects true absence of noise or robust normalization masking low-amplitude jitter
Exact cause of minor slopes in refs 1 and 3—could be residual trend from differencing or sensor drift; not actionable without labels
Boundary effects at pulse edges: whether rise/fall is truly instantaneous or limited by sampling rate

predictions.evidence: Pulse 3 begins at 1056, only 1 point after pulse 2 ends (~1055), compressing the inter-pulse interval from expected ~65 to ~1. This increases local event density; subsequent gap to pulse 4 is 76, indicating compensatory delay. Pulse shape remains normal, confirming frequency-type deviation (altered timing density), not shapelet or point.

A sharp, isolated impulse rising from baseline at 2416, peaking at ~5.0 (≈202% above normal amplitude 2.47) at 2419, and returning to baseline by 2422. Contrasts with learned normal pattern: normal pulses are flat-topped rectangles of width ~33 and amplitude ~2.47; this lacks a plateau and is globally extreme within the segment.

Four complete pulses occur in 201 points (period ≈50.25), versus learned period 98. Plateau duration ~15 pts (vs normal ~33), inter-pulse gaps ~31 pts (vs normal ~65). Amplitude, baseline, and edge sharpness remain normal—only cadence and duty cycle deviate, matching frequency definition.

subtask_history.goal: Inspect a global overview and characterize the dominant pattern and deviations.
subtask_history.summary: A global overview plot of [0, 5093] confirms a dominant periodic rectangular pulse train (period ≈98, amplitude ~2.47, plateau ~33 pts, zero baseline), consistent with reference memory. One high-confidence anomaly is identified: a narrow impulse spike at [2411, 2413] (peak ~5.0, ≤2 pts wide), isolated amid otherwise normal pulses and incompatible with downsampling artifacts, phase shifts, or truncation. No other deviations, trends, or structural breaks are observed. The sub-task goal—characterizing dominant pattern and deviations—is fulfilled; no further non-redundant evidence actions remain.

subtask_history.goal: Inspect a detail-scale window around the strongest unresolved overview candidate.
subtask_history.summary: The strongest unresolved overview candidate (spike near index 2412) was inspected via detail Plot over [2265, 2558], revealing a narrow high-amplitude impulse at ~2419 (amplitude ~5.0 vs normal ~2.47, width ~5–6 pts vs normal ~33), inconsistent with the learned rectangular pulse motif. A subsequent Compare against reference 2 at 3P scale ([2270, 2563]) refined the anomaly interval to [2413, 2419] (confidence 0.92, shapelet type), verified by x-axis ticks and curve timing (rise ~2413.2, peak ~2416.0, fall ~2418.8). Both tools confirmed isolation, amplitude excess (>100% above 90th percentile), lack of plateau, and incompatibility with phase shift, truncation, or sampling artifacts. The Mark action was executed on [2413, 2419] with decisive evidence; no unresolved uncertainty remains.

Neighboring pulses remain normal, confirming isolation. Verified via detail Plot and reference-based Compare against drift-free ref 2: rise begins ~2413.2, peaks at 2416.0, returns to baseline by ~2418.8. Incompatible with phase shift, truncation, or sampling artifact given strict rectangular normal motif.

subtask_history.goal: Inspect a detail-scale window of a normal-looking 3-cycle segment far from the known anomaly to verify global pattern consistency.
subtask_history.summary: A detail-scale inspection of [1000, 1294]—chosen to verify global consistency of the rigid normal rectangular pulse pattern—revealed two candidate anomalies: (1) a frequency-type cadence deviation (1056–1140, confidence 0.85) due to abnormally short inter-pulse gap (~20 pts vs expected ~65), and (2) a shapelet-type plateau distortion in pulse 3 (1106–1130, confidence 0.82), with shortened high phase (~25 vs 33 pts) and non-flat descending top, confirmed against drift-free reference ref 2. The shapelet anomaly was Marked as genuine, given the zero-noise, exact-period normal model rules out sampling jitter for >25% width reduction and slope. The frequency candidate remains unmarked but supported; residual uncertainty persists about whether the cadence irregularity is independent or linked to the shapelet event. No other deviations found in this segment.

mark.evidence: The second pulse (centered at ~1109) exhibits a shortened high plateau (~25 points vs nominal 33) and a non-flat, slightly descending top edge—deviating from the normal motif of instantaneous rise, flat plateau (≈1/3 cycle), and instantaneous fall. Rise and fall edges remain near-vertical, ruling out point or trend anomalies; the deviation is confined to the plateau morphology within one cycle. Verified via detail Plot and reference-based Compare against drift-free ref 2: plateau begins at 1106 (rise completes), ends at 1130 (drop begins); ticks at 1109 and 1146 confirm positioning. Minor sampling misalignment (≤1 index) cannot explain an 8-point shortening (>25%) or slope.
